#   kind: phrasal (English verb + particle -> one Greek verb), verbprep (verb + preposition: frame "obj" = the PP's noun
#         becomes the object, "prep:<greek>+<case>" = the verb fixes the Greek preposition), state ("be" + adjective
#         with a person subject: frame "verb" = the Greek verb replaces be + adjective, "mid" = its middle voice, "adj" =
#         this Greek adjective is the predicate), realia (no Attic word: the nearest hypernym, confidence Check,
#         rules_grc_notes.md decision 1), verb (a fixed choice for a frequent English verb; frame "past" = only in
#         the past tense), durative (imperatives and infinitives of this verb take the present stem: continuing or
#         general action, decision 8; every other verb takes the aorist for a single act; a state verb of the kind
#         "state" in the past: imperfect when durative, else aorist), perfect (C16: the perfect active of this Greek
#         verb has the intransitive / passive sense: "the clock is broken" -> κατέαγεν), pp (C16: a fixed prepositional
#         or adverbial phrase, source = preposition + determiner + noun as written in lower case: frame "adv" = the
#         Greek adverb, "prep:<greek>+<case>" = the Greek preposition + the noun (" def" = with the article), "ptc" =
#         the nominative participle agreeing with the subject, after the verb), weekday (C16: day name -> the god's
#         name in the genitive + ἡμέρα, "Ἄρεως ἡμέρα"; frame = the day's ordinal counted from Sunday for the
#         alternative "τρίτη ἡμέρα"), light (C18: a light verb or verb + object idiom, source = verb lemma + object
#         noun lemma: the noun is the verb's meaning and is not translated, "make a mistake" -> ἁμαρτάνω; frame "mid" =
#         the middle voice, "obj:<prep>" = the noun of that prepositional phrase is the Greek verb's object), subject
#         (C18: the verb chosen by its subject, source = subject noun + verb lemma: "sun rise" -> ἀνατέλλω); phrasal rows
#         may have frame "mid" / "pass" (the middle / passive voice: "wake up" -> ἠγέρθην).
#   verb rows, frame (C16): "nonfinite" = used instead of the main row when the verb is an infinitive, a subjunctive,
#         a future, or inside a subordinate clause / indirect question ("go" -> εἶμι: ἰέναι, ἴωμεν, εἶ); "sub" = used
#         inside a subordinate clause only ("before she comes" -> πρὶν ἥκειν).
#   C21: subject rows may have frame "mid" (the middle voice: "the rain stopped" -> ἐπαύσατο) or "mid-pres" (middle in the
#         present system, active elsewhere: δύεται / ἔδυ); a subject row's voice overrides a Spanish "se" read as a
#         passive; verb rows may have frame "mid" (the middle: "touch" -> ἅπτομαι + gen), "impers" (an impersonal weather
#         verb: "it is snowing" -> νίφει; a Spanish "nieva" read as an imperative is a statement) or "thing" (only with an
#         object that is a thing: "bring the water" -> φέρω); state rows may have frame "pass" (the passive: λυπεῖται,
#         ἐλυπήθη); kind noun (a fixed noun used only when greek.vpl has the lemma, else the realia row of the same source).
#   C29: verb rows may have frame "clause" (only when the verb has a that / que clause or an infinitive: "esperar que"
#   C31: verb rows may have frame "noobj-mid" (the middle voice whenever the verb has no object, places allowed: "hid
#         behind the door" -> ἐκρύψατο); state rows may give "adverb(s) + verb" ("right" -> ὀρθῶς λέγω: ὀρθῶς λέγεις).
